name: Example: Computing the Eigenvalues of a Matrix With At Most One Distinct Eigenvalue
problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/5ca3e07cfbe9e5d4956b1eab4393601f2a78b0b067d17312e71cbac993e28a86.png)
worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $B-\lambda I\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/fdbcc62870aefab6214b2f24f53e9bc5654e5386639d4bc328dff3769aff2b45.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det(B-\lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-0\cdot 0 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $B$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda=4,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation. 

**Note:** We also say that $\lambda=4$ has an **algebraic multiplicity** of $2.$
